# Proof bundle fixtures

Committed proof bundles the verifier tests run against.

| File | `t` | Subject | Signed? |
| ---- | --- | ------- | ------- |
| `appendix-d-item.json` | 20 | item | yes (illustrative key) |
| `entropy-nist.json` | 30 | entropy_nist | yes (illustrative key) |
| `entropy-stellar.json` | 31 | entropy_stellar | yes (illustrative key) |
| `entropy-bitcoin.json` | 32 | entropy_bitcoin | yes (illustrative key) |
| `item.json`, `item.cbor` | 20 | item | yes |
| `block.json`, `block.cbor` | 10 | block | yes |
| `item-bigint.json` | 20 | item | no — hand-built, needs `--skip-signatures` |

Only `item-bigint.json` is unsigned: it exists to exercise the safe-integer
guard over an `s.d` carrying a value beyond 2^53, so its signature was never
computed. Every other fixture verifies with the signature check enabled.

## The three entropy bundles

`entropy-nist.json`, `entropy-stellar.json` and `entropy-bitcoin.json` are
generated by [`gen_entropy_fixtures.exs`](gen_entropy_fixtures.exs) and consumed
by [`../../entropy_fixture_test.go`](../../entropy_fixture_test.go).

They exist because every other subject type had a signed artifact and the
entropy path did not: it was covered only by hand-built bundles that must run
with `--skip-signatures`, which removes the Ed25519 proof-signature check
(Appendix E.16) — the one check that makes a proof a proof.

All three are leaves of one shared Merkle tree, committed by one shared block
with one Stellar (`t=40`) and one Bitcoin (`t=41`) commitment, so each inclusion
proof is a real sibling path.

### What they do and do not establish

- **E.16 runs and passes.** The signature is real, over the real
  `SHA-256(0x61 || payload)` of the bundle's own values.
- **E.17 does not.** The signing key is the fixed, published illustrative seed
  (32 bytes of `0x42`, key id `f2c39df9`) that
  `truestamp-v2/whitepaper/proof_vectors.exs` signs the Appendix D vector with.
  It is not in Truestamp's keyring, so **Key Binding reports `skip`** — correct,
  expected, and the same behaviour `appendix-d-item.json` has.
- **The entropy values are illustrative and deliberately unresolvable
  upstream.** The observed values are deterministic digests of fixed label
  strings and the indices name pulses, ledgers and blocks that do not exist. A
  real E.21 re-fetch therefore finds nothing to compare, which the verifier
  grades `skip`, never `fail`. Committing real upstream values would couple
  these bytes to live network state and rot when NIST retires a chain or Horizon
  resets.

Because the illustrative Stellar/Bitcoin transactions are not on chain either, a
fully online `truestamp verify entropy-nist.json` reports Key Binding and
Stellar Commitment as failures. Verify these fixtures with `--skip-external`, as
the tests do.

### Regenerating

The generator needs the production `Jcs` canonicalizer from the
[`truestamp-v2`](https://github.com/truestamp/truestamp-v2) repo (assumed to be
a sibling checkout). From the root of this repo:

```sh
elixir -pa ../truestamp-v2/_build/dev/lib/jcs/ebin \
  internal/verify/testdata/fixtures/gen_entropy_fixtures.exs
```

The script gates every write behind a self-check: it re-derives each bundle from
the emitted map alone (its own `ts`, `pk`, `s`, `b`, `cx`), verifies the
signature over that re-derivation, and asserts that each signature **fails**
under the other two entropy type codes. A generator bug raises instead of
writing a bad fixture. It writes only into this directory.

Cross-check the result with the independent Elixir reference verifier, which
must report `VERDICT: PASSED` for each:

```sh
elixir ../truestamp-v2/whitepaper/verify_proof.exs \
  internal/verify/testdata/fixtures/entropy-nist.json
```

### Properties the tests depend on

Keep these true if you change the generator:

1. The signature payload uses the bundle's **own** `t`. The three bundles differ
   in that byte, so a payload built with a hardcoded `t` verifies for at most
   one of them — invisible to everything except a real signature check.
2. `s.d` matches the shape `internal/verify.parseEntropySubject` reads, so the
   report renders entropy detail instead of blanks. NIST nests under `pulse`
   and its `outputValue` is 64 bytes (128 hex characters), the beacon's width.
3. `s.id` is a UUIDv7 (entropy observations), never a ULID (items), and its
   embedded milliseconds are at or before `b.id`'s.
4. `s.mh` is the `0x22` hash of the empty metadata map — the constant Appendix
   C.4 publishes.
5. All three bundles share one block and one pair of commitments.
